previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with end-stage multiple myeloma, myelodysplastic syndrome, COPD, and a neobladder, was admitted for altered mental status and somnolence. Initial evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with Enterococcus sensitive only to vancomycin, prompting a switch from cefepime. His confusion improved with treatment and hydration, though it waxed and waned. Hypercalcemia was present but resolved with IV fluids. Imaging showed no acute intracranial process, stable abdominal aortic aneurysm, and improvement in prior lung opacity. Hip X-ray revealed severe osteoarthritis and lytic lesions consistent with myeloma progression. He was discharged home with a plan to return for continued IV vancomycin, with stable mental status and no acute complications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with multiple myeloma, s/p auto-SCT (___), 
myelodysplastic syndrome, recurrent hypercalcemia, COPD, CAD , 
AF, CHF (EF 50%), CKD (Cr 1.6), h/o bladder ca s/p radical 
prostacystectomy ___ with neobladder (straight cath 2x/day), 
admitted with altered mental status and entercoccal UTI. 
Patient's health declined over the course of admission from 
progression of multiple myeloma, and ultimately expired.
.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES
# Encephalopathy: Admitted with altered mental status, thought 
to be multifactorial, secondary to hypercalcemia, UTI, 
aspiration pneumonia and disease progression. With IV fluids and 
Lasix, calcium trended down. He was treated with vancomycin for 
enterococcal UTI, also empirically with Zosyn for aspiration 
pneumonia. IgG rose to 6126 with elevated circulating plasma 
cells, which indicated progression of disease. Patient became 
increasingly somnolent and delirious from end-stage disease. The 
patient was started on a morphine drip with boluses as needed, 
and he was comfortable and surrounded by family when he died.
.
# Multiple myeloma: Patient did not improved in response to 
treatments during this admission.  Prior to admission, he last 
had chemotherapy with Velcade ___. While an inpatient, he 
received two doses of pamidronate 30 mg IV on ___ and ___.  
However, subsequently increased IgG levels showing progressive 
disease despite treatment. Plasma cells were also present on his 
peripheral smear, peaking at 22. He was given Velcade again on 
___, and treated with IV dexamethasone. Despite these 
treatments, patient's disease progressed, with worsening kidney 
function and somnolence.  For prophylaxis, he was continue on 
fluconazole and acyclovir until he was unable to swallow pills.
.
# Hypercalcemia: Elevated on admission, secondary to multiple 
myeloma. Hypercalcemia likely contributed to his initial altered 
mental status. Calcium levels trended down with pamidronate 30mg 
x2 doses, aggressive fluid resuscitation, Lasix IV, calcitonin, 
and dexamethasone 20mg x2 doses. Sunbsequently, they remained 
stably elevated, 8.9-9.5 (uncorrected).
.
# UTI: Patient with a baseline of chronic pyuria in the setting 
of neobladder, with urine culture growing enterococcus, 
sensitive to vancomycin.  He was continued on vancomycin 1 g IV 
q48 hours, until decision was made to focus on comfort-oriented 
care.
.
# Aspiration: with waxing and waning mental status, patient had 
ongoing problems with aspiration of PO diet.  In the ED, he was 
noted to be hypoxic, with an initial PaO2 of 67 on RA.  With 
nebulizers and supplemental oxygen, oxygenation improved during 
admission, although the patient continued to aspirated, as 
demonstrated on CXR's and swallowing study.  He was treated 
empirically for aspiration pneumonia with Zosyn, until the 
decision was made to focus on comfort-oriented care.
.
.
# Oral thrush: Noted on exam during this admission, and was 
treated with fluconazole IV, then PO.  Discontinued at time of 
transition to comfort-oriented care. 
. 
.
CHRONIC ISSUES
# COPD/Emphysema/restrictive lung disease: Stable throughout the 
hospitalization. Pt was continued on albuterol neb prn and 
tiatroprium and fluticason-salmeterol
.
# Myelodysplastic syndrome: Atypical WBC on differential. 
Thrombocytopenia stable. Patient's counts were monitored and 
transfused as needed.
.
# CAD: BB held on last admission due to bradycardia, though it 
is unclear whether re-started as outpatient. He was continued on 
metoprolol 25 mg daily and monitored for bradycardia. Continued 
metoprolol until he was unable to swallow pills.
.
# Chronic systolic heart failure: EF 50% in ___, was euvolemic 
on exam.
.
# Chronic kidney disease, stage 3: Creatinine increased during 
hospitalization likely due to hypercalcemia secondary to 
multiple myeloma. 
.
# Depression: Patient was continued on SSRI, until he was unable 
to swallow pills.
.
# Gout: Patient was continued on allopurinol, until he was 
unable to swallow pills.
.
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: None

INDICATION:  End-stage multiple myeloma, status post auto stem cell

FINDINGS:  This study is slightly limited secondary to patient motion.  There
is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, acute large vascular territorial
infarction, hydrocephalus, edema, or shift of normally midline structures. 
Periventricular white matter hypodensities are consistent with chronic small
vessel ischemic disease.  Prominence of the ventricles and sulci are
consistent with age-related involutional change.  Bilateral cavernous carotid
and vertebral artery calcifications are noted.  Mucosal thickening is seen
within the left maxillary sinus, as on the prior study from ___. 
There may be a new air-fluid level within the left maxillary sinus as well. 
The remainder of the visualized portions of the paranasal sinuses and mastoid
air cells are well aerated.  A diffusely mottled appearance of the calvaria
likely relates to known underlying multiple myeloma.  The orbits are grossly
unremarkable.

air-fluid level is suggestive of acute on chronic sinusitis.

INDICATION:  History of end-stage multiple myeloma as well as numerous

question of aspiration.  Evaluate for pulmonary edema and lung metastases.

(4:192).

Enlargement of the main pulmonary artery, measuring up to 3.2 cm, is not
significantly changed compared to ___.  Extensive thoracic
aortic calcifications are again seen.  There are also severe coronary artery
